text:
Consider the hydrated ions of $Ti^{2+}, V^{2+}, Ti^{3+}$, and $Sc^{3+}$. The correct order of their spin-only magnetic
moments is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As we know that

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$
where n = no. of unpaired electrons i.e. greater the no. of unpaired electron more will be the spin-only magnetic moments.

. Electronic configuration of the given transition
metal ions are

$Sc^{3+} (Z = 21) = 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}$

$\therefore$ n = 0

$Ti^{2+} (Z = 22) = 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}3d^{2}$

$\therefore$ n = 2

$Ti^{3+} (Z = 22) = 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}3d^{1}$

$\therefore$ n = 1

$V^{2+} (Z = 23) = 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}3d^{3}$

$\therefore$ n = 3

 So the correct
increasing order of magnetic moment is

 $Sc^{3+} < Ti^{3+} < Ti^{2+} < V^{2+}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
Consider the statements S1 and S2

S1 : Conductivity always increases with decrease in the concentration of electrolyte.

S2 : Molar conductivity always increases with decrease in the concentration of electrolyte.

The correct option among the following is :
options: Both S1 and S2 are wrong
S1 is correct and S2 is wrong
Both S1 and S2 are correct
S1 is wrong and S2 is correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know conductivity (k) = $\frac{G}{V}$

V = volume

When concentration decreases volume increases and when volume increases then conductivity (k) decreases.

So, we can say S1 is incorrect.

We know that,

$λ_{m}=\frac{k}{c}$

where

$λ_{m}$ = molar conductivity

k = conductivity

c = concentration

So, when concentration decreases molar conductivity increases.

So, we can say S2 is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
A bacterial infection in an internal wound grows as $N'(t) = N_{0} \exp (t)$, where the time t is in hours. A dose of antibiotic, taken orally, needs 1 hour to reach the wound. Once it reaches there, the bacterial population goes down as $\frac{dN}{dt}=-5N^{2}$. 
What will be the plot of $\frac{N_{0}}{N}$
vs. t after 1 hour?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dN}{dt}=-5N^{2}$         for  t > 1 hr

'N' increases upto 1 hr and then start decreasing after 1 hr.

$\therefore$ $\frac{N_{0}}{N}$ will increase after 1 hr.

Therefore option (D) is correct.

text:
Consider the following statements

(a) The pH of a mixture containing 400 mL of $0.1 M H_{2}SO_{4}$ and 400 mL of 0.1 M NaOH will be approximately 1.3

(b) Ionic product of water is temperature dependent.

(c) A monobasic acid with $Ka = 10^{–5}$
 has pH = 5. The degree of dissociation of this acid is 50 %.

(d) The Le Chatelier's principle is not applicable to common-ion effect. 

The correct statements are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(a) Equivalance of strong acid = 0.1 $\times$ 2 $\times$ 400 = 80

Equivalance of strong base = 0.1 $\times$ 400 = 40

$\therefore$ [$H^{+}$] of mixture = $\frac{80-40}{800}$ = $\frac{1}{20}$

$\therefore$ pH = $-\log [H^{+}]$ = $-\log \left (\frac{1}{20}\right )$ = 1.3

(b) Ionic product of water increases with
increase of temperature because ionisation
of water is endothermic.

(c) 
[IMG]

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{α}{(1-α)}$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = 0.5

$\therefore$ Degree of dissociation($α$) = 50%

text:
At 300 K and 1 atmospheric pressure, 10 mL of a hydrocarbon required 55 mL of $O_{2}$ for complete
combustion, and 40 mL of $CO_{2}$ is formed. The formula of the hydrocarbon is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{x}H_{y} +$ $\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )O_{2}$ $\to$ xCO$_{2} +$ $\frac{y}{2}H_{2}O$

According to the above equation,

1 mL of hydrocarbon = x mL of $CO_{2}$ is produced

$\therefore$ 10 mL of hydrocarbon = 10x mL of $CO_{2}$ is produced.

According to question,

From 10 mL of hydrocarbon 40 mL of $CO_{2}$ is produced.

$\therefore$ 10x = 40

$\Rightarrow$ x = 4

Also from the above equation,

1 mL of $C_{x}H_{y}$ react with $\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )$ mL of $O_{2}$.

$\therefore$ 10 mL of $C_{x}H_{y}$ react with 10$\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )$ mL of $O_{2}$.

According to question,

10$\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )$ = 55

$\Rightarrow$ $40+\frac{10y}{4}=55$

$\Rightarrow$ y = 6

$\therefore$ Hydrocarbon is $C_{4}H_{6}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text: The principle of column chromatography is :
options: Differential adsorption of the substances on the solid phase.
Differential absorption of the substances on the solid phase.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The principle of column chromatography is based on the differential adsorption of substances on the solid phase. This means that different substances in a mixture will interact with the solid stationary phase to different extents. Some substances will adsorb more strongly to the solid phase and will therefore move more slowly through the column, while others will adsorb less strongly and will therefore move more quickly. This differential adsorption allows for the separation of the substances in the mixture.

So, the correct answer is :

Option C : Differential adsorption of the substances on the solid phase.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

text:
At room temperature, a dilute solution of urea is prepared by dissolving 0.60 g of urea in 360 g of water. If the
vapour pressure of pure water at this temperature is 35 mm Hg, lowering of vapour pressure will be.
(molar mass of urea = 60 g mol$^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that,

$w_{$solute$} = w_{$urea} = 0.6 gm

$w_{$solvent$} = w_{H2}O = 360 gm$

$p^{o} = 35$

We know, 

lowering of vapour pressure 

$\Deltap = x_{$solute} $\times$ $p^{o}$

= $\frac{n_{urea}}{n_{urea}+n_{H2O}}$ $\times$ $p^{o}$

= $\frac{\frac{0.6}{60}}{\frac{0.6}{60}+\frac{360}{18}}$ $\times$ 35

= $\frac{10^{-2}}{20}\times 35$

= 0.017

solution.body:
With excess HI both ether linkages are cleaved.
$(i) Ar–O–CH_{3}$: the aryl C–O bond is not cleaved (partial double-bond character), so $I^{–}$ attacks the methyl carbon and the ring keeps an –OH group (phenol) while $CH_{3}I$ is released.
$(ii) Ar–CH(CN)–O–CH(CH_{3})_{2}$: after protonation of the ether oxygen, the bond between oxygen and the benzylic carbon breaks (the benzylic position is the one activated by the ring) and $I^{–}$ bonds to that carbon, giving Ar–CH(I)–CN; the isopropyl part leaves as $(CH_{3})_{2}$CHOH, which excess HI converts to $(CH_{3})_{2}$CHI.
Major product: $3-HO–C_{6}H_{4}–CH(I)–CN, i.e$. option (C).

text:
The species that can have a trans-isomer is :

(en = ethane-1, 2-diamine, ox = oxalate)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{2+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA}){}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{2}]$: each en spans two cis positions, and the two $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ ions can be either adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans), so a trans isomer exists.


[IMG]

In $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}(\mathrm{ox})]{}^{+}$ the three chelate rings fill all six positions, each spanning cis positions, so no trans form is possible; the four-coordinate $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{en})\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]$ and $[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{en})\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]$ have only one arrangement each, because en must span adjacent positions.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

solution.body:
Methanol is a weak base and a weak nucleophile, while as a polar protic solvent it assists ionisation of the secondary bromide; the reaction is therefore solvolysis by the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ path, not E2, which needs a strong base.

Loss of $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ gives the secondary carbocation $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{C}^{+}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

A 1,2-hydride shift from the adjacent tertiary carbon converts it into the more stable tertiary carbocation $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}\mathrm{C}^{+}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

Methanol attacks this cation and loss of $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ gives 2-methoxy-2-methylbutane, $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OCH}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.


[IMG]

The unrearranged ether in (D) is not the major product because the hydride shift is faster than capture of the secondary cation.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
